findings.issue: The desktop hero photo still has lettering printed into it ('…Sunlit Days', 'and summer-ready prints', and 'Shop Swimwear' / 'Explore the Collection' pills). It shows through behind our live H1, lead and button, so the hero reads as two overlapping layers of text, with dead buttons under the live one; the last pill is also cut by the trust bar (reported before; still unchanged in these shots; the phone crop happens to miss the lettering).
findings.reference: The competitor's hero photo is a clean shot with no lettering. The only text on it is the live eyebrow, title, lead and two buttons.
findings.fix: Give /custom-swimwear-printing/ a hero photo with no lettering in it. Take the lettered photo out of the photo pool until it is regenerated without the text.

findings.issue: On phones the wide-variant factory photo still keeps its desktop strip ratio (about 2.3:1). It shrinks to a band about 150px tall under a long run of text, too small to read (reported before; still unchanged).
findings.reference: The competitor's phone photos in text sections (the handover/mock-up image) run full width at a near-square or 4:3 ratio.
findings.fix: In reference.css at the stacked breakpoint, give the .block--split[data-variant="wide"] media aspect-ratio: 4 / 3 with object-fit: cover.

findings.issue: Two neighbouring sections of the same shape still stand one under the other: m7 (process) and m8 (iconList) both set their rows of short items as a list beside the heading (reported before; unchanged).
findings.reference: Site rule: of two neighbouring sections made of short-item rows, the template sets only one of them as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: When a process list and an iconList are neighbours, have the template give m8 the other iconList arrangement (items in columns under the heading).

findings.issue: After the photo band, m12 (proof), owner-testimonials and related all still sit on white, so three neighbouring plain sections do not alternate. This shows at both widths; only the FAQ after them is tinted (reported before; unchanged).
findings.reference: The competitor alternates beige and white or navy bands from section to section. Site rule: the template alternates white and --section-tint between neighbouring plain sections.
findings.fix: Include testimonials and relatedPages blocks in the template's white/tint alternation so the run reads white, tint, white.

findings.issue: On phones the three-option comparison table still cuts its fourth column ('Pigm… with und…', 'Digit… pigm… print…') off at the right edge. The label column is squeezed until 'White or pastel areas' stacks one word per line. The last repair deliberately kept the sideways scroll for charts of three or more options, so this stays open.
findings.reference: On phones the competitor shows comparisons as stacked panels (the 'Plain colours' / 'Prints' cards), with nothing cut off sideways.
findings.fix: Give the comparison chart (.chart-comparison) a stacked phone layout: one card per option column, its rows as label/value pairs, instead of the sideways scroll.

findings.issue: On phones two of the centred trust-bar labels end in a lone orphan word ('SUBLIMATION QUOTE / TIME', 'BULK PRODUCTION / TIME').
findings.reference: The competitor's short centred labels and captions break into even lines with no single word left alone.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give the trust-bar label (.trust-bar label element) text-wrap: balance so each label splits into two even lines.

findings.issue: On phones the H1 breaks the compound 'In-House' across lines ('Printing with In- / House Sublimation'), which reads like a hyphenated word break in the title.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone H1 ('Your first / collection, / step by step.') breaks only between whole words.
findings.fix: Write the title's compound with a non-breaking hyphen ('In‑House', U+2011) so the fitted title wraps before 'In-House', not inside it.
